title: PyKotor writes ANSI debug output to stdout, which destroys an MCP session
body: On first import and on every Installation build, PyKotor logs through the root logger with ANSI colour codes. Under MCP, stdout is the JSON-RPC transport, so a single stray byte makes the client fail to parse and the server dies in a way the user never sees. Measured directly on 2026-09-12 while smoke-testing the library. Contained in kio.py: every PyKotor call runs inside a quiet() context that redirects stdout to a buffer and pins the root logger to CRITICAL. Verified afterwards with a real JSON-RPC handshake launched from C:\WINDOWS\system32 with no environment, exactly as Claude Desktop launches it.
evidence:
DEBUG(root): Loading BIFs from chitin.key at 'D:\SteamLibrary\...'
-> after containment:
INIT OK  server: {'name': 'kotor-forge', 'version': ''}
TOOLS: 24 registered
STDIO HANDSHAKE CLEAN -- no transport corruption

title: PyKotor creates a logs/ directory in the process working directory at import
body: Claude Desktop launches MCP servers with the working directory set to C:\WINDOWS\system32, where creating a directory raises WinError 5 -- and PyKotor prints that failure to stdout, triggering the transport hazard above a second time. kio.py chdirs into the forge's own logs directory before the first PyKotor import.
evidence: Failed to init 'logs' dir in cwd 'C:\WINDOWS\system32': [WinError 5] Access is denied: 'logs'

title: MCP SDK 2.x renamed FastMCP to MCPServer
body: The sibling servers er-forge and ac6-forge are pinned to mcp 1.29.1 and import mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP. On mcp 2.2.0 that import raises, with a message pointing at mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer. The .tool() decorator and .run() signatures were checked and are drop-in identical, so KOTOR Forge imports either. The two older servers will break the day their venvs are upgraded -- worth knowing before it happens rather than after.
evidence:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp.server.fastmcp'. This is mcp 2.x,
where FastMCP was renamed to MCPServer

title: PyKotor round-trips this install's core formats byte-identically
body: Read-write-compare was run against live resources pulled out of the game, not against synthetic fixtures. Seven probes covering 2DA, three GFF template types and SSF all returned byte-identical output. The in-process NSS compiler produced valid NCS from source. dialog.tlk parsed at 136,329 entries. This is the gate that licenses the write tools: a format that does not round-trip is a format the server refuses to write.

title: PyKotor 2.3.12 cannot read a [CompileList] at all -- and that breaks HoloPatcher too
body: The most consequential bug found. ModificationsNSS.__init__(self, filename, *, replace=None, ...) makes replace keyword-only, but PyKotor's own ConfigReader passes it positionally. Somebody added the *, to the subclass and missed the one caller; the base class still takes it positionally. [CompileList] compiles NSS scripts and a large share of real TSLPatcher mods have one, so every such mod fails to install -- not just through this server, but through HoloPatcher itself. Contained by nssfix.py, a runtime shim that lives in our code rather than site-packages, so a pip upgrade cannot silently revert it, and that becomes a no-op once upstream fixes the signature. Because holopatcher.exe is a separate process that would load PyKotor unpatched, installs run through our own launcher instead.
evidence:
holopatcher --install --console  ->  rc=7
TypeError: ModificationsNSS.__init__() takes 2 positional
arguments but 3 were given

after nssfix:
Compiling 'kf_verify.nss' and saving as 'kf_verify.ncs'
nwnnsscomp.exe was not found, using the built-in compilers...
The installation is complete with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

title: Installation caches the override file list, so reads go stale right after a mod install
body: Installation snapshots override/ when it is built, and it is cached for the life of the process. After a successful install put a patched spells.2da and feat.2da into override/, twoda_query still returned the stock row counts. The wrong read is the small half of this. The real danger is that twoda_edit would then load the vanilla table, edit that, and stage a file that silently erases whatever the other mod did -- exactly the failure this server exists to prevent. Contained twice over: the cache is dropped after every deploy, revert and mod install, and reads now check override/ on disk case-insensitively before consulting the cache at all.
evidence:
after install, before the fix:
  feat.2da -- 245 rows   (stock)
after the fix:
  feat.2da -- 246 rows x 91 cols, 1 matched
  245  KF_VERIFY_FEAT

title: override/ is not the whole attack surface -- dialog.tlk is patched in the game root
body: TSLPatcher's [TLKList] appends to dialog.tlk in place, in the game root, not in override/. Backup originally copied only override/, so a mod install appended string-table entries that no revert could undo. Two test installs left dialog.tlk 120 bytes and 2 entries larger than stock with nothing in our own backups to restore from; it was recovered from HoloPatcher's own backup inside the mod folder, and a pristine copy is now archived. Backups now cover dialog.tlk, swkotor2.ini and swplayer.ini; revert restores them and says so, and warns loudly when the chosen backup predates the feature and therefore cannot undo a TLK patch.
evidence:
GAME-ROOT FILES  (patched in place by mods, outside override/)
   dialog.tlk    9.7 MB  !! PATCHED (stock 9.7 MB, +120 bytes)

after the fix:
   dialog.tlk    9.7 MB  stock
   swkotor2.ini  1.5 KB  stock
   swplayer.ini   677 B  stock

title: A real TSLPatcher mod installs, takes effect, and reverts cleanly
body: A valid mod was constructed -- real 2DAs pulled out of the game, a real append.tlk, an NSS script, a file to copy -- exercising [TLKList], [2DAList], [CompileList] and [InstallList]. It installed with 5 patches and 0 errors, and the edits were then read back through the engine's own resolution order rather than merely confirmed to exist as files. Reverting restored the install byte-for-byte: 60 override files all matching their recorded hashes, dialog.tlk back to 136,329 entries, feat.2da back to 245 rows.

title: Tool output must be pure ASCII, because drive.py prints to a cp1252 console
body: A single U+26A0 warning sign in a tool's output raised UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character and killed a verification run mid-flight. MCP itself is UTF-8 JSON and would have been fine, but the non-MCP CLI prints straight to a Windows console. Every source file is now pure ASCII and asserted so. er-forge is pure ASCII for the same reason.
evidence:
File "...\encodings\cp1252.py", line 19, in encode
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character
'\u26a0' in position 491

title: Achievements are hardcoded in the executable -- and cheating cannot disable them
body: The usual answer to this is folklore, so the binary was disassembled instead. There are 57 achievements, not 37. Exactly one achievement_%d format string exists, with one cross-reference, inside a single award function; scanning for every call to it finds 59 call sites carrying IDs 0-56. Not one of them tests a cheat flag. The CHEATUSED string appears only in save-serialisation and save-screen GUI code -- it is a cosmetic label on the save thumbnail. All 5,120 shipped scripts were parsed and none can award an achievement. So the console, save editing and mods cannot disable anything.
evidence:
achievement_%d  @ 0x9868A0   (1 xref)
AwardAchievement @ 0x4010A0   -> SteamUserStats
59 call sites, IDs {0..56}, no gaps, zero cheat-flag guards
5,120 .ncs parsed: highest engine routine = 876 (vanilla range)

title: givecredits does not merely spare the credits achievement -- it is what awards it
body: The console command is givecredits; there is no addcredits. Tracing the handler shows it passes through the cheat gate into SetPartyGold, and the 10,000-credit achievement check lives inside that setter. Only eight callers of SetPartyGold exist in the whole engine, two of them the merchant buy and sell paths -- so every route to credits funnels through the same check. A quirk found on the way: the handler floors any amount of 99 or less at 99.
evidence:
console "givecredits"  (0x7ABA90)
  -> cheats gate       (0x7AB0D0)
  -> GetPartyGold      (0x5812E0)
  -> SetPartyGold      (0x581330)
       +-- cmp [gold], 10000 -> AwardAchievement(33) @ 0x581395

title: About forty achievements are keyed to dialog.tlk line IDs -- which is why mods break them
body: A dispatch function binary-searches its input against 46 hardcoded constants between 77,670 and 135,903. Each is an exact string reference; looked up in this install's dialog.tlk they resolve to real lines -- Mira joining the party, the Handmaiden joining, the pazaak Golden Card, Nihilus' mask. The engine is watching for a specific line of text, by number, being shown. Rewrite that dialogue node, or append to the TLK so the line carries a different id, and the achievement silently never fires. This explains every reported mod incompatibility, and it means purely graphical mods are provably safe -- they cannot touch DLG or TLK at all. The remaining ~17 achievements are engine state checks hooked into setters and are immune to dialogue mods.
evidence:
ID 19 <- StrRef 115525  "[Mira has joined the party...]"
ID 27 <- StrRef 117029  "[The Handmaiden has joined your party...]"
ID 23 <- StrRef 113927  "Here, take this Golden Card..."
ID 53 <- StrRef 100776  "Look upon his face, then bring me the mask."

title: PyKotor cannot re-serialise a savegame losslessly, so the save editor never tries
body: A load-then-save through PyKotor's save API, with no edits at all, rewrites four of the five files and shrinks savegame.sav by about 19 KB on both of the real saves tested. Even one file at a time, GFF read-then-write is not byte-identical for partytable.res or globalvars.res. So the save editor parses the GFF binary header directly, locates one field's value bytes, and patches them in place -- the same prove-then-write discipline er-forge uses for param offsets. A write is refused if the field label is ambiguous, if the field is stored indirectly, if the file length changes, if more than four bytes differ, or if the field no longer holds the value that was just read.
evidence:
no-op load+save:
  savegame.sav   986,505 -> 967,781   (-18,724 bytes)

surgical patch, credits 0 -> 250,000:
  bytes changed  3
  size           8,899 -> 8,899  unchanged
  savegame.sav   SAME  sha 0f260504a7a2
  globalvars.res SAME    savenfo.res SAME    screen.tga SAME
  oracle refusal test: refused correctly

title: The cutscenes are natively 2.353:1, and this machine's monitor is 2.400:1
body: KOTOR II's .bik movies are 640x272 -- cinemascope. On a 16:9 display they letterbox heavily, which is why upscale packs exist that bake 16:9 black bars into the files. On a 3840x1600 panel they very nearly fill the screen. That inverts the usual advice: the pack with baked-in bars would put a 2.353:1 image inside a 16:9 box inside a 2.40:1 screen, losing real resolution on all four sides. The 3440x1440 rescale set, at 2.389:1, is within about one percent of both the source and the display.
evidence:
vanilla .bik          640 x 272   = 2.353:1
primary display      3840 x 1600  = 2.400:1
best available pack  3440 x 1440  = 2.389:1

title: TSL still ships K1's Large body meshes and simply never points at them
body: Searching this install turns up pfbal, pfbbl, pfbcl through pfbjl and the male equivalents -- the complete Large body set K1 used for its three body sizes. TSL kept the assets and pointed every appearance row at the Medium variants, apparently a schedule cut. So a fuller-figured character needs no new art: clone an appearance row and repoint its equipment slots at the Large meshes. Three caveats, all needing an in-game check: slots k, m and n have no Large variant, the dancer slot is single-size, and the Large underwear texture does not ship.

pfbcs..pfbjs  pfbcm..pfbjm  pfbcl..pfbjl   <- armour + robes

title: Two large Deadly Stream downloads fired together, and one silently died at 8 KB
body: The cutscene pack ships eight variants behind one modal. Clicking the 22.22 GB archive and the 2.31 GB companion back to back looked fine in the browser: no error, no warning text on the page, both rows acknowledged. On disk the small one completed and the large one sat at 8,192 bytes and never moved. Nothing in the DOM said so -- only a filesystem check did. Retried alone, the same archive pulled at a sustained 37.5 MB/s and finished in about ten minutes. The rule that came out of it: pull large archives one at a time, and confirm the .crdownload is actually growing before moving on to the next thing.

title: Steam Cloud is SHA-tracking the savegames, which puts it in direct conflict with the save editor
body: The save tools patch partytable.res surgically -- a credits change touches exactly three bytes and every other file in the save is left byte-identical. That precision is worth nothing if something else rewrites the save afterwards, so the Steam side was checked rather than assumed. remotecache.vdf records a SHA-1 per file for every save, and the saves themselves live in the game folder's cloudsaves\ directory. A patched file no longer matches its recorded SHA, so Steam can offer to restore its own copy and quietly undo the edit. The last recorded sync was 2025-02-05, so the cloud copy is already months stale -- restoring it would cost real progress. Steam Cloud has to be off for appid 208580 before any save editing.
evidence:
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\userdata\138831487\208580\remotecache.vdf  (2,962 B)
  "cloudsaves/138831487/000001 - AUTOSAVE/SAVEGAME.sav"
    size 62493  sha c06277e08c7c8657104ccb93042cb38a1642fe95  syncstate 1
  + GLOBALVARS.res, PARTYTABLE.res, pifo.ifo, savenfo.res -- each SHA-tracked
  remotetime 1738732687 = 2025-02-05

title: Every staged archive was CRC-tested, not size-checked
body: 45 archives, 30.2 GB, pulled from two hosts over a couple of hours. A truncated CDN transfer is indistinguishable from a complete one by size alone, and the place it surfaces is halfway through a TSLPatcher run -- after the patcher has already written to shared 2DAs and dialog.tlk. So each archive was opened and CRC-tested, with the exit code checked per file. WinRAR is the archiver on this machine so it is the one that certifies the library, and only exit code 0 counts as a pass: exit code 1 is “warning”, and WinRAR also returns it when handed a file that is not an archive at all -- a real MANIFEST.md came back rc 1 during the smoke test, so treating 1 as a pass would have certified garbage.

title: The TSLRCM download was not waiting on a click -- Chrome had cancelled it
body: The first read of this was wrong, and the correction only came from going to the system of record. It looked like a held download awaiting a Keep press, so that is what was reported. Chrome's own downloads table says otherwise: target tslrcm2022.exe, state CANCELLED, interrupt 41 = USER_SHUTDOWN. Chrome was closed while the confirmation was outstanding and that killed the entry, so the advice pointed at a control that no longer existed. The same record clears up a second misreading: the danger flag is DANGEROUS_FILE, which is Chrome's label for the file type -- what every .exe gets -- and not a Safe Browsing detection. There is no DANGEROUS_CONTENT, URL or HOST on it. One orphaned .crdownload survives at exactly the published byte count with an MZ header, but neither WinRAR nor 7-Zip can open it, which rules out SFX and NSIS and means its contents cannot be checked without running it. So it gets re-downloaded rather than promoted, and the third-party Google Drive re-host linked in a forum review stays rejected: a silent difference in the most load-bearing mod in the build would not surface as an error, it would surface as an unexplainable broken install hours later.
evidence:
id 81
  target     tslrcm2022.exe
  bytes      0 of 137,947,655
  state      CANCELLED
  danger     DANGEROUS_FILE   (file TYPE, not a detection)
  interrupt  41 = USER_SHUTDOWN

orthan on disk: 137,947,655 B, header b'MZ'
  winrar t  rc 1 -- cannot read as an archive
  7z l      rc 2 -- Cannot open the file as archive

title: 3C-FD is not a GUI to click through -- it is a self-extracting PowerShell bundle
body: The plan was to drive its interface. Running it once instead unpacked a 3cfd\ folder into the game directory containing patcher.ps1, a separate GUI script, a build-signature file, and one declarative JSON per patch -- hex find/replace blocks with ?? wildcards. patcher.ps1 takes -File, -Patch, -DryRun and -Backup, detects “already applied” by searching for the replace pattern rather than trusting a flag, and refuses outright on a find/replace length mismatch. So the whole step ran headless, dry-run first, and verifiable afterwards -- the forge's own doctrine, handed over for free by the mod author. One trap: its -ApplyAll would have been wrong, because the patches folder holds KOTOR 1, GOG and Borderless variants side by side with the four we wanted.

title: A binary patch that changes no bytes of length made forge_scan report a patched exe as stock
body: forge_scan judged the game-root files by size, which works for dialog.tlk because TSLPatcher appends to it. 3C-FD does the opposite: it is a search-and-replace patcher that rewrites shader strings and one header flag in place. After nine blocks landed, the executable was exactly the same 6,588,416 bytes and the scan cheerfully called it stock. Same blind spot as the earlier dialog.tlk gap, found the same way -- by checking the tool's answer against the thing it was describing. forge_scan now hashes the executable and reports one of three states, and swkotor2.exe was added to the backed-up root files, because without it forge_revert could not have undone step one of the build at all.

title: Not one mod in the library touches dialog.tlk, so all 57 achievements survive
body: About 40 of the 57 achievements fire when a specific dialog.tlk StrRef is displayed, with the ids hardcoded in the executable -- so a mod that appends to that table shifts the ids and kills them silently. Rather than trust the achievement-safe reputation of each mod, all eleven tslpatchdata folders in the library were parsed: every one declares a [TLKList] section and every one is empty. The one mod that does ship a dialog.tlk ships three complete replacement tables, and all four verified achievement StrRefs read back identical in each -- its 46 extra entries are appended, not inserted, so nothing below them moves.

title: appearance.2da is edited in place by eleven separate patcher runs
body: The survey turned a vague worry into a countable one. Eleven TSLPatcher runs write to appearance.2da: the Community Patch, both Kreia mods, Fit Handmaiden, and Player & Party Underwear which is six separate runs, one per character. TSLPatcher resolves that correctly only if each run reads the previous run's output, so they go strictly in sequence against the live install. The trap sits right next to them: Fit Handmaiden ships a loose 694-row appearance.2da at its folder root, next to its own patcher. Stock is 671 rows. Copied into override/ mid-sequence it would erase every other mod's rows -- the exact failure this server exists to prevent.

title: 539 filenames are shipped by more than one mod, so install order is the conflict resolution
body: override/ is flat and last writer wins, which means the order decides every collision whether or not anyone thought about it. Across 4,325 loose files, 539 filenames are contested. The largest pair is Upscale+ Character Fixes against UCO REDUX LITE at 499 files -- and the guide's instruction to install Upscale+ last of the textures turns out to be exactly what that number requires. One worry evaporated on inspection: three separate loading-screen packs each ship a loadscreens.2da, and all three are byte-for-byte identical.

title: Build on PyKotor in-process, not on a pile of external executables
body: PyKotor is the only thing in the KOTOR ecosystem that reads and writes every format the game ships, from one language, one process. Every alternative is either read-only for some formats (xoreos-tools has no model or walkmesh support), GUI-only (KOTOR Tool, MDLedit), or requires another runtime (MDLOps needs Perl, KotorBlender needs Blender). Shelling out buys nothing and costs typed objects and structured errors. It is LGPL, so linking is fine.

title: The Aspyr lightsaber-hilt breakage is a renderer bug, not a format change
body: The Aspyr build breaks lightsaber hilt texture mods and removed some fog effects. The community fix works by moving the hilt mesh into a separate model referenced by the blade model, which points at an extra shader applied at render time rather than at anything different in the MDL on disk. File-level tooling is therefore unaffected -- but any hilt mod is a known-suspect install, and Workshop-installed mods should stay out of a manual mod build entirely.

title: Treat every KOTOR path as case-insensitive
body: The Aspyr builds disagree with themselves about TexturePacks versus texturepack, and Vortex's own extension lists the lowercase singular. PyKotor ships a CaseAwarePath type and HoloPatcher advertises case-insensitive path handling as a headline feature -- both are responses to the same mess. Assume nothing about casing anywhere in this game's directory tree.

title: Body proportions cannot be changed from 2DA values alone
body: There is no scale column in appearance.2da. The only columns matching *scale are weaponscale, wing_tail_scale and the two helmet scalers -- all attachment props. height looks like a candidate and is not one: a rancor has height 1 and a human female player character has height 1.6, so it feeds camera framing and targeting rather than mesh size. Real proportion changes mean editing the MDL in KotorBlender, or repointing slots at a differently-shaped mesh that already exists.

title: A full mod build and a complete achievement run are mutually exclusive -- do two passes
body: Not because of cheating, which costs nothing, but because several Tier 1 mods in the canonical build rewrite exactly the dialogue that carries trigger string references. The clean answer is sequencing rather than compromise: run the achievements first on restoration plus every graphical, upscale, lightsaber and appearance mod -- all provably safe -- with the console enabled, since cheats satisfy the skill, credit, level and Force-power checks directly and genuinely speed the run. Achievements once earned are permanent. Then install the heavy narrative layer for the story playthrough.
